note: Generated from the web engine. Do not hand-edit. Regenerate with: cd web && CRUCIBLE_WRITE_GOLDEN=1 npx vitest run golden-powder

scenarios.name: single-grain-falls
scenarios.why: One grain, no contention. Pins down fall speed and the resting row.

scenarios.name: column-collapses
scenarios.why: A vertical column. Exercises the bottom-up scan: processed top-down the whole column would collapse in a single tick instead of falling at a sane speed.

scenarios.name: pile-forms-on-floor
scenarios.why: A block of sand onto a bedrock floor. The shape of the resulting pile is decided entirely by the diagonal-slide rules and the per-row scan direction flip.

scenarios.name: slides-off-a-shelf
scenarios.why: Sand landing on a narrow bedrock shelf must shed off both shoulders.

scenarios.name: inverted-gravity-sand-rises
scenarios.why: Gravity up flips the vertical scan to top-down. Sand must pile on the ceiling.

scenarios.name: zero-gravity-sand-still-settles
scenarios.why: With gravity at zero the direction comes from the fallback branch, which sends granular solids downward anyway. Guards that fallback.

scenarios.name: no-sideways-drift
scenarios.why: A single grain on a flat floor, run long. The per-row alternating scan direction exists to stop exactly this grain from walking sideways forever.

scenarios.name: tall-stack-settles
scenarios.why: Enough sand to fill several rows, so cells repeatedly contend for the same space and the visited mask is load-bearing.

scenarios.name: water-pools-in-a-basin
scenarios.why: Water levelling out. Exercises viscosity, cohesion and the erosion reaction, which draws from the random stream on every water cell every tick.

scenarios.name: water-erodes-a-sandbank
scenarios.why: The erosion reaction specifically: flowing water must carve sand and carry it downstream.

scenarios.name: lava-cools-into-obsidian
scenarios.why: Lava losing heat until it crosses the 700C vitrification threshold, with no water involved.

scenarios.name: thin-water-cap-vitrifies-lava
scenarios.why: The hardest fidelity target in the whole port. A shallow water cap over a small lava pocket: the water flashes off almost immediately, so the lava must keep shedding heat to its steam and obsidian neighbours to cross the threshold. With weaker cooling coefficients it stalls near 1100C and oscillates forever. Guards the web fix for bug 2.

scenarios.name: obsidian-crust-never-remelts
scenarios.why: The same geometry run far longer. Once the fight resolves nothing may re-melt: the residual steam and condensation loop must settle rather than re-quenching forever.

scenarios.name: fire-spreads-through-wood
scenarios.why: Ignition by flammability, fire decaying to smoke, and smoke expiring. The core fire loop.

scenarios.name: ice-melts-and-freezes-water
scenarios.why: Two directions at once: ice melting above zero, and ice spreading through cold water.

scenarios.name: acid-dissolves-a-wall
scenarios.why: Acid corrosion, including the resistance roll. Glass is immune, stone resists partly, wood not at all, so all three paths through the check are exercised.

scenarios.name: spark-seeks-water-along-wire
scenarios.why: Electricity: the scoring scan, conductor load flood fill, the hop, and water being flashed to steam. Also covers the branch that returns without consuming the spark.

scenarios.name: c4-detonates
scenarios.why: The explosion path end to end: three blast zones, ballistic embers and the smoke plume. By far the heaviest consumer of random numbers, and the draw order is intricate.

scenarios.name: gunpowder-chain-reaction
scenarios.why: Explosions triggering further explosions, which is where a draw-order error compounds fastest.

scenarios.name: plants-drink-and-grow
scenarios.why: Plant growth consuming water, plus seeds germinating on dirt through a declarative rule.

scenarios.name: salt-dissolves-into-salt-water
scenarios.why: The declarative interaction path: salt meeting water becomes nothing and makes the water salty.

scenarios.name: portals-teleport
scenarios.why: Portal pairing, the random choice of exit, and the search for a free cell beside it.

scenarios.name: fan-drives-smoke
scenarios.why: Fan rotation from the lifetime slot, the pressure it adds, and the momentum it imparts.

scenarios.name: virus-infects-everything
scenarios.why: Virus spreading through solids, which converts a large region and stresses the reaction loop.

scenarios.name: clone-and-void
scenarios.why: A duplicator feeding a singularity: one creates matter every tick and the other erases it.

scenarios.name: copper-pipes-heat
scenarios.why: The heat-pipe pass: copper moving temperature without moving mass, and leaking it into contact.

scenarios.name: sealed-steam-pocket-detonates
scenarios.why: Pressure build-up in a sealed container until it lets go. The only path that reaches the pressure detonation check, which fires at most once per four ticks.

scenarios.name: wind-blows-gases-sideways
scenarios.why: The wind pass, which is the only place outside movement that relocates cells.

scenarios.name: shaken-world-settles
scenarios.why: The shake gesture: a velocity kick to every loose cell, decaying over the following ticks.

scenarios.name: honey-and-oil-and-mercury-stratify
scenarios.why: Three liquids of different density and viscosity in one container. Buoyancy sorting plus the viscosity and cohesion gates, all of which draw conditionally.

scenarios.name: laser-stops-at-bedrock
scenarios.why: A beam must not reappear on the far side of a bedrock wall. The loop used to continue past bedrock to the next distance instead of stopping.

scenarios.name: liquid-cannot-cross-a-thin-wall
scenarios.why: Two sealed tanks separated by a one-cell wall. Water used to reach two cells sideways without checking the first, so it hopped straight through and drained.

scenarios.name: lightning-ignites-oil
scenarios.why: Oil used to be classed as 'wet', so a spark treated the most flammable liquid in the game as water and could never set it alight.

scenarios.name: spark-dies-beside-mercury
scenarios.why: Mercury counts as wet but is never converted, and the spark used to re-stamp its own lifetime every tick — an immortal spark that also seeded a new one forever.

scenarios.name: fan-stops-at-a-wall
scenarios.why: A fan blowing into stone used to match neither branch of its loop, so it carried on and pressurised cells on the far side of the wall.

scenarios.name: explosion-plume-follows-inverted-gravity
scenarios.why: The smoke plume used to be hardcoded upward, so under inverted gravity it fired into the ground.

scenarios.name: custom-rule-spawns-and-heats
scenarios.why: spawnElementId and tempChange are declared on an interaction rule but the original never read either, so custom elements could not produce a third element or release heat. Also guards that a rule doing nothing no longer freezes the particle.

scenarios.name: everything-at-once
scenarios.why: A deliberately chaotic world run long, mixing every subsystem. If any single reaction draws at the wrong moment, the two engines diverge here even when every focused scenario above still agrees.
